title: Production sweep stamps every attempt entry with an empty `at` timestamp (`now_iso` is "")
evidence:
sweep.gleam:164: `Ok(run(db_conn, deps, "", sentry, default_batch_limit))`
sweep.gleam:702-705:
```
fn outcome_entry(outcome: ChannelOutcome, at: String) -> json.Json {
  json.object([
    #("at", json.string(at)),
```
sweep.gleam:533: `at: now_iso,`
messages.gleam render_attempt_line: `<> email_client.escape_html(entry.at) <> ": "`
detail: Production passes now_iso="" (only the due-SELECT substitutes now()); every sweep-stamped attempt entry therefore persists "at":"" in the attempts JSONB, in terminal results re-emitted via parse_attempts, and renders as ": email, skipped" in the §8.3 warm-handoff email. Tests pass "" too and never assert `at`, so nothing catches it.
recommended_fix: When now_iso is "", stamp entry timestamps from a Gleam-generated ISO string (gleam_time is already a server dep) or RETURNING now()::text from the guarded updates, before building entries.

title: sweep.gleam duplicates result.gleam's attempt decoder for the same {at, channel, outcome, detail} shape
evidence:
result.gleam:
```
fn attempt_decoder() -> decode.Decoder(AttemptRow) {
  use at <- decode.optional_field("at", "", decode.string)
  use channel <- decode.optional_field("channel", "", decode.string)
  use outcome <- decode.optional_field("outcome", "", decode.string)
  use detail <- decode.optional_field("detail", "", decode.string)
```
sweep.gleam:
```
fn attempt_decoder() -> decode.Decoder(AttemptEntry) {
  use at <- decode.optional_field("at", "", decode.string)
  use channel <- decode.optional_field("channel", "", decode.string)
  use outcome <- decode.optional_field("outcome", "", decode.string)
  use detail <- decode.optional_field("detail", "", decode.string)
```
detail: The lens asked: yes, this is a duplication. Both decoders parse the same attempts JSONB shape with identical optional_field defaults; result.gleam re-emits it as json.Json, sweep.gleam as List(AttemptEntry). Same failure-to-[] semantics.
recommended_fix: Add one shared decoder for messages.AttemptEntry (e.g. in messages.gleam) and have result.parse_attempts and sweep.parse_attempts_entries both use it.

title: standard_sender const duplicated between send.gleam and the new notification_dispatch.gleam
evidence:
send.gleam:34: `const standard_sender: String = "RightTenantry <noreply@app.righttenantry.ie>"`
notification_dispatch.gleam:18: `const standard_sender: String = "RightTenantry <noreply@app.righttenantry.ie>"`
detail: The diff introduces a second copy of the same sender identity literal. The two can drift (a renamed sender would silently split landlord-facing mail streams). Verified both are in use (:131 send, :616 dispatch).
recommended_fix: Define the sender once (email_client is the natural home, already imported by both) and reference it from send.gleam and notification_dispatch.gleam.

title: sweep.gleam re-implements messages.first_name (already public, subtly different)
detail: messages.first_name is public, already imported by sweep.gleam, and trims first; the sweep's private copy does not (an all-whitespace contact_name yields the raw name). DRY violation per project conventions.
recommended_fix: Replace the sweep's private first_name with messages.first_name calls (import it alongside the other messages bindings).

title: Warm-handoff email renders a fabricated reminder-2 entry instead of the actual outcomes appended this tick
evidence:
sweep.gleam:528-539:
```
  let attempts =
    parse_attempts_entries(row.attempts)
    |> list.append([
      AttemptEntry(
        at: now_iso,
        channel: "email",
        outcome: "reminder_2",
        detail: "T+96h reminder",
      ),
    ])
```
detail: The row's actual append (outcomes_to_json of the real send results, e.g. "delivered"/"skipped"/"failed" plus the SMS outcome) can differ from the synthesized "email/reminder_2" line, so the landlord email's log can contradict the append-only attempts JSONB — e.g. claiming a sent reminder when the send was skipped.
recommended_fix: Build the render from this tick's actual outcomes (parse the same entries passed to sweep_advance) or re-read attempts after the advance, so the email mirrors the row's log.
